properties.name: FIELD CONFIRMATION: prose_currency fired on every status move in one dev_storyflow session (2026-09-06, 0.48.0) and was right three times — three capability descriptions still described a sketch after the build, each rewritten on the spot
properties.statement:
dev_storyflow, 2026-09-06 on 0.48.0, in their words: 'When set_verification_status and set_capability_status moved a node planned → passing/verified, the reply carried a prose_currency block quoting the description written under status: planned and asking whether it still read true. It caught a real one: the item-4 capability's description still described a sketch (`y_level: 2`, a coherence rule that flags…) while the build had used axis/level and a validate_edge rule. I revised the description on the spot. That is exactly the kind of check that makes the graph trustworthy rather than merely populated — please keep it.' Later the same day: 'fired again on every status move and was right every time I checked it' — the item-5 and item-6 capability descriptions were still sketches after the build and were rewritten; and on two planned capabilities the root-cause pass found the design's claim wrong ('engine validates no edge' was already true one layer down), which prose_currency surfaced when the status moved. THREE stale descriptions caught in one day by the check, in the field, on a build two versions old.

THE ONE ASK, recorded as an idea: the excerpt is cut at 240 characters, and in the item-4 case the stale words sat past the cut, so the reader fetched the node anyway. Proposed: quote the whole description when under ~1 KB, otherwise the first sentence and a diff-worthy tail. dec:idea-prose-currency-quotes-enough-to-judge-without-a-second-read.
